players.product: Nebula autonomous lab, RAC robotics, and Ginkgo Datapoints

quarterly_data.signal: Nebula expanded to 105 robotic RACs after adding 50 RACs and returning to experiments in roughly three weeks. It runs 24/7 and on an average day handles about 30 unique scientist-submitted protocols across more than 100 devices; the autonomous layout uses about one-third the space of comparable manual labs.
quarterly_data.figure: 105 RACs; +50 in ~3 weeks; ~30 protocols/day; 24/7; ~1/3 lab space

quarterly_data.signal: ADME-One launched as an automated domestic CRO service at $199 for a five-assay Tier-1 panel versus stated Western CRO pricing of $2,000-$5,000 and Chinese CRO pricing of $1,000-$2,500. The service added 16 customers in its first six weeks and management is extending the system toward plate-based chemistry and anaerobic synthesis.

Q2 revenue was $20 million, down 48%, and adjusted EBITDA was negative $36 million, including $14 million of excess leased-space carrying cost. Cash burn was $45 million in Q2 and $93 million in H1; full-year cash-burn guidance remains $125 million-$150 million. Cash and equivalents were $302 million, plus $87 million of restricted cash.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $20M; adjusted EBITDA -$36M; H1 burn $93M; FY burn $125M-$150M; cash $302M

quarterly_data.signal: Ginkgo was selected to build autonomous labs for MIT, Caltech, the University of Maryland and Northwestern, adding academic deployments to its Pacific Northwest National Laboratory program. Hardware revenue is recognized at delivery and installation, followed by recurring software and support revenue.

contracts.signal: Management identified Bayer as a customer of Ginkgo's large, multi-year automated biological research services that use its lab infrastructure.
